primitives.name: DirectedGraph
primitives.statement: There is a directed graph G=(V,E).
primitives.operational_definition: Vertices V and directed edges E with source/target.

primitives.name: FinitePathRule
primitives.statement: A path is a finite composable sequence of directed edges; zero-length paths are allowed.

definitions.name: PathComposition
definitions.statement: Compose compatible paths by finite sequence concatenation.

definitions.name: EmptyPath
definitions.statement: For each vertex v, epsilon_v is the zero-length path at v.

definitions.name: PathQuotient
definitions.statement: A quotient identifies paths under an equivalence relation.

claims.statement: Zero-length paths are left and right identities for path concatenation.
Every directed graph with the finite-path rule generates an associative compositional process system with identities.
Arbitrary path equivalence does not guarantee well-defined quotient composition; a composition congruence is required.
Physically useful coarse-graining may correspond to selected composition congruences on process spaces.

observables.name: PathLength
observables.definition: Number of primitive edges in a finite path.

falsifiers.condition: Produce finite compatible edge sequences for which list concatenation is not associative.
Show quotient composition remains representative-independent under an equivalence relation that is not composition-compatible.

metadata.purpose: Test derivation of composition structure from finite directed paths.
